"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:5120: the "open question about what to do" feature.

What it does: it switches on inside a question or deliberation about how or what to
proceed, such as "I don't know what to do", "how to", "which way", "should I". It is
strongest on the wh-word that opens such a question ("how" most, then "what", "whether",
more weakly "which" and "where") and on the word right after that wh-word when the
question continues into an action or manner ("to", "do", "way", "far", "much", "many",
"should", "be", "can", "one"). A question mark gets a small value. Everywhere else it sits
at the bulk level of about -0.04.

Why: its output direction promotes words such as "how", "which", "should", "best" and
"choice" in the model's next-token distribution, so it is a "I am choosing how to act"
signal. Only the wh-word and the following action word are predictable from the text;
most of its variance is a diffuse, context-dependent bulk that this program does not model.
"""

READS = ()

BASE = -0.04
WH = {"how": 1.8, "what": 0.8, "whether": 0.7, "which": 0.2, "where": 0.2}
ACTION = {"to", "do", "does", "should", "be", "way", "far", "much", "many", "can", "one"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in WH:
        return None, WH[word]
    if word == "?":
        return None, 0.3
    if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        if prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() in WH and word in ACTION:
            return None, 2.0
    return None, BASE

"""Layer-15 MLP unit-5121 write (layers.15.mlp.down_proj:5121), a weak, mostly unexplained signal.

What it does: its activation is a small, signed value (std about 0.32) that is almost
unpredictable from the text. The simple structure that exists, and that this program
keeps:
  - the first token of each document is silent (0);
  - on other tokens it sits near -0.05, and is more negative when the token repeats
    something already seen earlier in the same document (copying / repeated text,
    about -0.09 vs -0.05), and least negative on a fresh letter-only word (about -0.03).
This explains well under 1% of its variance; the rest is context the program cannot read.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# mean activation by (token is a letters-only word, token already seen in this document)
LEVEL = {
    (True, False): -0.028,  # fresh word
    (True, True): -0.052,  # repeated word
    (False, False): -0.051,  # punctuation, digits, spaces, new
    (False, True): -0.087,  # punctuation, digits, spaces, repeated
}
WORD = re.compile(r"\s?[A-Za-z]+")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the set of token ids already seen in the current document
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    seen = set() if new_doc else carry
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    repeated = token in seen
    seen.add(token)
    if new_doc:
        return seen, 0.0  # a document's first token is silent
    is_word = WORD.fullmatch(prefix.token_strings[-1]) is not None
    return seen, LEVEL[(is_word, repeated)]

"""Predict this MLP down-projection unit's activation from position in its document.

Almost all of the unit's activation is noise: no token identity, token class,
repeated-token or context-window feature predicts it (out-of-sample variance
explained below 0.02). The one real pattern is at the start of a document: the
unit leans positive for the first few tokens (about +0.1 at positions 1-3) and
the lean fades to the usual slightly negative level (about -0.02) by roughly
position 20. This program predicts that fade and nothing else.

Position is counted within a document: the first token is position 0. The
carry holds the current token's position, reset where the document changes.
"""

READS = ()

BASE = -0.02  # typical activation away from document starts
BUMP = 0.1  # extra lean at position 1
DECAY = 0.85  # the lean shrinks by this factor each position


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    pos = 0 if new_doc else carry + 1
    if pos == 0:
        value = 0.0
    else:
        value = BASE + BUMP * DECAY ** (pos - 1)
    return pos, value

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 5124 (down_proj component), as a code-layout detector.

In plain terms: this component is quiet on most text. It responds to the
layout of source code. It is strongest on a closing bracket that ends a line
("}\\n", "});", "},") when the document has no opening bracket still unclosed
before it, i.e. a block whose opener is out of view. It is weaker on closing
brackets that sit mid-line, and weakly positive on the indentation whitespace
in front of code lines (tabs more than spaces). It is pushed clearly negative
on the end-of-tool-call tags. Everything else is about zero.

The bracket depth is counted over the document so far, from its first token,
and resets at each new document in the row.
"""

import re

READS = ()

OPENERS = "{(["
CLOSERS = "})]"
TOOL_TAGS = ("</tool_call>", "</tool_response>")

# value when the bracket depth is 0 (no unclosed opener in view), and when it is not
CLOSE_NL = (5.8, 0.3)  # a closing bracket that ends a line
CLOSE_MID = (1.6, 0.1)  # a closing bracket inside a line
INDENT_TAB = (0.9, 0.4)  # whitespace containing a tab
INDENT_SPACES = (0.25, 0.2)  # two or more spaces
TOOL_TAG = -3.0


def _value(text, depth):
    """Activation for one token's text, given the unclosed-bracket depth before it."""
    k = 0 if depth == 0 else 1
    stripped = text.strip().rstrip(";,")
    if text in TOOL_TAGS:
        return TOOL_TAG
    if stripped and set(stripped) <= set(CLOSERS):
        return CLOSE_NL[k] if "\n" in text else CLOSE_MID[k]
    if re.fullmatch(r"[ \t]+", text) and "\t" in text:
        return INDENT_TAB[k]
    if re.fullmatch(r" {2,}", text):
        return INDENT_SPACES[k]
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (unclosed bracket depth, document label of the last token)
    depth, doc = carry if carry is not None else (0, None)
    doc_now = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc_now != doc:
        depth = 0  # a new document starts with nothing open
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = _value(text, depth)
    for ch in text:
        if ch in OPENERS:
            depth += 1
        elif ch in CLOSERS:
            depth = max(0, depth - 1)
    return (depth, doc_now), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 5125: a lexical detector.

This component is quiet on most tokens (about -0.06) but swings strongly negative on
structural tokens: the markup of chat and tool-call transcripts (`<tool_call>`, `{"`,
`name`, `user`, `</think>`), markdown headers, code fences, separators and code
keywords, and label words that open a heading or a note. Opening brackets are
moderately negative. Clause-opening connectives and a few code return or arrow tokens
are mildly positive. The program looks at the current token's group, and nudges the
value when the previous token was itself structural, and doubles the structural values
inside a <tool_call> block. Everything else gets the baseline. The group means were
fitted on training rows (R^2 about 0.08 on a held-out half of 4M positions); a lookup
of every token's own mean reaches about 0.15, so most of the variance is not explained
by any simple concept.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

AGENT_MARKUP = {
    "<|im_start|>", "<|im_end|>", "<tool_call>", "</tool_call>", "<tool_response>",
    "</tool_response>", "</think>", '{"', "name", "user", "assistant", "arguments",
}
CODE_SCAFFOLD = {
    "```", "###", "##", "####", "#####", "===", "---", "print", " print", "def", " def",
    "func", "function", "console", "cd", "/workspace", "workspace", "class", "const",
    "\tif", "\tfor", "import", "echo", "try", "while", "case", "export", "package",
    "var", "fn", "let", " let", "execute", "type", "diff", ".log", ".out",
}
LABELS = {
    "Command", "Current", "Note", "See", " See", "References", "Example", " Example",
    "Figure", " Figure", "Fig", "Math", "Page", "Question", "Solution", "ATION", "PASS",
    "RUN", "Read", "Click", "Input", " Input", "Expected", "Category", "Location",
    "Review", "Posts", "June", "External",
}
BRACKETS = {"[", " [", "@", " @"}
CONNECTIVES = {
    " return", "\treturn", "->", " (-", "Hmm", "Even", "Many", "While", "However",
    "Although", "Since", "Similarly", "As", "But", "Perhaps", "Some", "Both", "Each",
    "Most", "Non", " Non",
}

# Mean activation of each group, fitted on training rows.
GROUP_MEAN = [
    (AGENT_MARKUP, -2.57),
    (CODE_SCAFFOLD, -2.96),
    (LABELS, -4.19),
    (BRACKETS, -1.40),
    (CONNECTIVES, 0.71),
]
BASELINE = -0.06
# Inside a tool-call block the structural groups are about twice as negative.
TOOL_SCALE = 2.0
# Shift when the previous token was structural (any group except connectives).
AFTER_STRUCTURE = -0.7
STRUCTURAL = AGENT_MARKUP | CODE_SCAFFOLD | LABELS | BRACKETS


def _group(token: str) -> float | None:
    for group, mean in GROUP_MEAN:
        if token in group:
            return mean
    return None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Activation at the newest token: its group's mean, else the baseline.

    The carry says whether we are inside a <tool_call> block (reset at each document):
    there the group means are doubled, since structure is more negative in tool calls.
    """
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_strings) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    in_tool = False if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    if token == "<tool_call>":
        in_tool = True
    elif token == "</tool_call>":
        in_tool = False
    value = _group(token)
    if value is None:
        value = BASELINE
    elif in_tool:
        value *= TOOL_SCALE
    if not new_doc and prefix.token_strings[-2] in STRUCTURAL:
        value += AFTER_STRUCTURE
    return in_tool, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 5126: a diffuse, unexplained activation.

What it is: the component's activation is almost entirely (hidden unit 5126 of layer 15's MLP)
x 0.22; other hidden units add little. That unit's own value is not explained by anything below.
Its value is a dense, roughly symmetric signal (std about 0.34, mean about 0.015) that
is not a function of the current token (per-token means explain about 2% of variance on
held-out text), of the previous token, of the position in the document, of character classes,
or of the model's own surprisal or entropy. Its causal importance is ~0: switching the
component off changes the model's next-token predictions almost nothing.

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical value everywhere, the mean
activation. It captures the average level and none of the position-to-position variation,
so it explains essentially none of the variance. It is a placeholder, not an explanation.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.015


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 5127 (this component reads almost only that unit), as a word detector.

The component's activation is (x . V) * |U|, and its V vector is almost entirely one MLP
hidden unit, so its activation is that unit's value. It is large and positive on words that
link a second action or point onto the first, the way "and then", "In addition", "Moreover",
"并" ("and, also"), "然后" ("then") and "同时" ("at the same time") do. It is about 0 on most
tokens and mildly negative on a few chat and greeting openers ("assistant", "Hi", "Sure").

This program predicts that: a fixed value per connective word, a boost for "then" after
"and", and zero everywhere else. It reads only the newest token.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Typical activation on the word itself, from the component's own values in the training data.
JOIN_WORDS = {
    # Chinese: joins an action or point to the one before it
    "并": 12.0, "並": 11.0, "并且": 12.0, "並且": 12.0, "，并": 12.0,
    "同时": 9.5, "然后": 9.0, "然後": 8.0, "随后": 9.0, "进而": 9.0, "而且": 8.0,
    "且": 6.5, "此外": 6.5, "从而": 5.0, "另外": 5.0, "后来": 3.8, "于是": 3.7,
    "还": 3.0, "又": 3.0, "再": 2.5, "以及": 2.0,
    # English: adds a further point, or sequences the next step
    "Moreover": 6.5, "Furthermore": 6.2, "Additionally": 4.7, "Finally": 4.6,
    "Meanwhile": 4.2, "Lastly": 3.7, "Plus": 3.2, "addition": 3.2, "Then": 2.9,
    "Also": 2.6, "Secondly": 1.8, "while": 1.5, "followed": 1.3,
}

# Weaker connectives: the same kind of word, with a smaller typical value.
WEAK_WORDS = {
    "also": 1.0, "after": 1.0, "well": 1.0, "However": 0.6, "however": 0.6, "yet": 0.8,
    "Yet": 1.2, "instead": 0.8, "Instead": 0.8, "Nevertheless": 2.4, "Consequently": 1.9,
    "otherwise": 0.9, "Otherwise": 0.9, "Further": 1.6, "plus": 0.9, "Together": 0.5,
}

# Mildly negative: chat-role tag, greetings and reply openers.
NEGATIVE_WORDS = {
    "assistant": -1.6, "born": -1.7, "Hi": -2.2, "Hello": -1.8, "Sure": -2.2,
    "Certainly": -2.5, "Dear": -1.7, "你好": -4.2, "import": -0.7,
}

VALUES = {**WEAK_WORDS, **JOIN_WORDS, **NEGATIVE_WORDS}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if word == "then":
        # "and then" is a stronger join than a bare "then"
        previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if prefix.position > 0 else ""
        same_doc = prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
        return carry, 3.8 if same_doc and previous in ("and", "And") else 1.8
    return carry, float(VALUES.get(word, 0.0))

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, rank-one component 5128: a near-silent, unstructured component.

What it does, in plain terms: its activation is a small, sign-mixed value (typical size
about 0.35) at almost every token, with rare large spikes (up to about 40 in magnitude in
training data) on scattered tokens. The token itself explains little: even a full
token-by-token lookup table explains about 1% of its variance, and token categories
(newlines, digits, punctuation, capitals, non-ASCII, code symbols) and whether the token
repeats earlier in its document explain essentially none. The only regularities found are
positional: the first token of each document is silent (about 0), and the second token of
a document is slightly more negative and spikes more often (about 13 times as often as
elsewhere). Everywhere else the program predicts the component's average, about -0.03.
"""

READS = ()

AVERAGE = -0.03  # mean activation over ordinary positions
SECOND = -0.04  # second token of a document: slightly negative, spikes more often


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # A row packs several documents; a new document starts where its label changes.
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    first_in_doc = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    if first_in_doc:
        return carry, 0.0
    if len(ids) == 2 or ids[-2] != ids[-3]:
        return carry, SECOND
    return carry, AVERAGE

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 5129: a diffuse, context-driven read-out with no
describable trigger.

What the component is: its activation is (hidden · V_c)·‖U_c‖, a linear read-out of the
layer-15 MLP hidden state along one direction. That direction is spread across thousands
of hidden units (the 40 largest hold only about 40% of its energy), so it is not one
neuron or one word. Its activation is roughly zero-mean noise, mean 0.037, std 0.31, with
slow drift inside a document (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.34) but no token, bigram, position,
repetition or genre rule that explains it: a per-token lookup explains about 2% of its
variance, and simple word-class and repetition features explain essentially none.
Its causal importance is ~0 everywhere (it never passes the 0.1 threshold), and switching it
off changes the next-token distribution by about 1e-6 nats per position, so it is inert.

What this program does: it predicts the component's average activation at every position,
the best constant in the mean-squared sense. Nothing about the text is used, so this is an
explanation of what is not explainable, not of a feature.

Main program: the value at each token is the constant MEAN_ACTIVATION.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.037
"""The component's mean activation over the eval-like sample (0.037; std 0.31)."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The activation at this position: the same constant, whatever the prefix."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:5130.

Its activation is almost unpredictable from the text. It is a dense, roughly Gaussian
signal (std about 0.32) whose contribution is tiny, and it is nearly all the same
neuron (hidden unit 5130 of layer 15's MLP). Token identity explains about 2% of its
variance, and no simple word class does better. The one clear regularity is where the
position sits in its document: the first token is exactly 0, the next few tokens dip
negative (about -0.15 just after the start), and the level drifts back up to about
+0.02 from roughly 30 tokens in. This program predicts that position profile and
nothing else.

Each document's position is counted from its first token. The carry holds the
current document label and the position so far, so a new document resets the count.
"""

READS = ()

# (first position in document, predicted activation from there on, until the next band)
BANDS = (
    (0, 0.0),  # the document's first token
    (1, -0.12),  # the next three tokens
    (4, -0.04),  # up to about the 15th
    (16, -0.01),  # up to about the 31st
    (32, 0.015),  # the rest of the document
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or doc != carry[0]:
        n = 0  # first token of a new document
    else:
        n = carry[1] + 1
    value = 0.0
    for start, level in BANDS:
        if n >= start:
            value = level
    return (doc, n), value

"""Predicts layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 5131 (activation = its hidden-unit read-out).

What the component is: a single rank-one read of layer 15's MLP hidden units, weighted
mostly on hidden unit 5131 but spread over thousands of others. Its activation is roughly
zero-mean noise (std 0.27) around a small negative offset (-0.045). Nothing simple predicts
the noise: no token identity, token class, position, document, or scalar summary of the
MLP hidden state explains more than a fraction of a percent of its variance.

What this program does, and only this:
  * the first token of each document (the one with no earlier token in its document)
    gets 0, which is where the component's activation sits (about -0.004);
  * digit tokens get a value near zero (about -0.005, versus about -0.05 elsewhere);
  * every other token gets the component's typical offset, -0.045.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL = -0.045  # the component's mean activation on ordinary tokens
DIGIT = -0.005  # mean activation on digit tokens
DOC_START = 0.0  # mean activation on a document's first token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        return carry, DOC_START
    if prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().isdigit():
        return carry, DIGIT
    return carry, TYPICAL

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 5132.

What it does, in plain terms: this component is mostly diffuse. Its value is
small and of mixed sign at almost every token, and no token identity, character
class or position explains the bulk of it. Its large values are rare, and two
recurring templates account for the part that is simple:

1. The word "of" in a knowledge-base triple, as in Wikidata-style lists
   ("Ronnie Hillman — instance of — Human", "X | instance of | Y"): value about +5.
2. The "ATION" that completes "OBSERVATION" in a tool response
   ("<tool_response> OBSERVATION: ..."): value about +3.

Everywhere else the program predicts the component's typical value, about -0.025.
It claims only these two templates; the rest of the variance is not explained.
"""

READS = ()

BASE = -0.025  # the component's typical value
INSTANCE_OF = 5.0  # " of" right after " instance", in the same document
OBSERVATION = 3.0  # "ATION" right after "OBSERV"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    value = BASE
    if len(toks) >= 2 and toks[-1] == " of" and toks[-2] == " instance":
        if docs[-1] == docs[-2]:
            value = INSTANCE_OF
    if len(toks) >= 2 and toks[-1] == "ATION" and toks[-2] == "OBSERV":
        if docs[-1] == docs[-2]:
            value = OBSERVATION
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 5133, seen through its down_proj component.

The component reads mostly the MLP hidden unit 5133 of layer 15 (its largest input
weight) and writes it back into the residual stream. Its activation is signed and
heavy-tailed (mostly within +-1, with rare swings to -20 and +7), and it is
mostly context-driven: no single token, previous token, word class, script,
document position or bag of nearby words explains more than a few percent of it.

The one lexical signal is the word " of": on average the unit goes negative there
(mean about -0.67 over 105k sampled occurrences, with spread about 1.8), while
every other token averages near 0. So this program predicts that mean on every
" of" and 0 elsewhere. It captures only about 1.5% of the variance on eval.
"""

READS = ()

OF_MEAN = -0.67  # mean activation on " of" over the sampled occurrences


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at this position: the mean on " of", 0 on every other token."""
    return carry, (OF_MEAN if prefix.token_strings[-1] == " of" else 0.0)

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:5134: a diffuse feature with no simple trigger.

This is one rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP down projection. It reads the MLP hidden state
through a direction V that is mostly hidden unit 5134 (about a third of its variance) plus many
small weights, and writes along a direction U that, read through the unembedding, promotes and
suppresses no clear set of tokens.

Its activation is dense, heavy-tailed noise around -0.04 (std 0.40, rare spikes near +/-10).
Nothing simple predicts it on held-out text: the token's identity, its neighbours, its character
class, a bag of recent tokens, or a shrunk per-token table each explain under 2% of its variance.
A few tokens lean one way (' vor' and ' cut' tend positive, '@@' and 'grep' negative), but each
has a wide spread.

So this program predicts the component's mean activation at every position. That is the best
constant under squared error. Its effect on the model is essentially the same as switching the
component off (kl_fraction about 0.99).
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.0375


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The component's activation at this position: its mean, whatever the prefix."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 5135: a diffuse, context-dependent readout with no simple concept.

Its activation is (MLP hidden state . V_c) * |U_c|. It is dense (about 0.3 std around 0.03),
but no token class, token identity, bigram or position explains more than a few percent of it.
The best simple description is its average level, so this program predicts that constant,
with the one clear exception that the first token of each document reads as zero.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.03  # average over the eval rows, about 0.033; the spread (std 0.3) is unexplained
DOCUMENT_START_ACTIVATION = 0.0  # the first token of a document reads as zero


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    starts_document = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, DOCUMENT_START_ACTIVATION if starts_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 5136: a diffuse readout with no readable trigger.

What it does: this component is silent on the first token of each document (its activation
there is ~0) and, everywhere else, takes a small value scattered around +0.017 (std 0.26).
Its activation is not tied to any token, position, or context feature we could find:
token identity, the previous token, coarse token classes (digits, CJK, Latin, punctuation),
position in the document, and the script mix of the surrounding row together explain well
under 1% of its variance. So the program predicts the component's average value, with the
document-start silence, and makes no claim beyond that.

Main program: `step` runs once per token. It returns 0 at a document's first token
(the model resets attention there), and the mean activation elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.017  # the component's average activation over training rows


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    return None, 0.0 if starts_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:5137, a weak token-kind detector.

What it does: predicts this component's activation from the kind of the current token.
  - closing brackets and closing quotes/backticks (")", "]", "}", '"', "”", "`", "’"): positive
  - digits (numbers, numbered labels such as "B1" or "2 4"): mildly positive
  - opening brackets and opening quotes ("(", "[", "{", "“"): negative
  - everything else (ordinary words, spaces, most punctuation): 0

Why: the component's output direction, read through the (tied) unembedding, promotes
"and", "both", "two" and "和" as the next token, so it tends to be active at the end of
an item that a coordinated pair or list may continue. Its activation, though, depends
mostly on context the token alone does not show, so this rule explains only a little
of it. A full token-identity table would explain about twice as much, and no
simple concept does better.
"""

READS = ()

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection component 5175: a weak chat-context signal.

What the component reads: its activation is a dot product of layer 15's MLP hidden
state with one direction, and that direction is dominated by hidden unit 5175 (about a
quarter of its variance; the rest is spread over thousands of small units). The
activation has mean about 0.08 and std 0.34, with per-token noise that no simple
feature captures. What is systematic:

  * It is higher inside a chat-template assistant reply than in user turns or plain
    text, and it keeps rising the further one is into a reply (about 0.3 after a few
    hundred tokens, against 0.08 in plain text). Right at the role word "assistant"
    it dips below zero.
  * It is higher on Han (Chinese/Japanese) characters and lower on punctuation,
    sentence ends and whitespace.

The program follows the chat template from the tokens alone: `<|im_start|>` opens a
turn, the next token `user` or `assistant` names it, `<|im_end|>` closes it, and each
new document starts with no turn open. It counts tokens since the role word and adds a
token-class offset. This explains about 1.5% of the variance; the rest is per-token
noise this program does not model.
"""

import regex

# Mean activation by chat role and by tokens into an assistant reply.
NONE_VALUE = 0.08  # plain text, outside any turn
USER_VALUE = 0.04  # inside a user turn
ASSISTANT_TABLE = ((3, 0.0), (10, 0.08), (30, 0.13), (100, 0.19), (300, 0.30))
ASSISTANT_DEEP = 0.32  # 300 or more tokens into the reply
ROLE_WORD_VALUE = -0.25  # the role word "assistant" itself

# Offsets by token class.
HAN_OFFSET = 0.05  # Han characters
PUNCT_OFFSET = -0.04  # punctuation, sentence ends, whitespace (no letters or digits)

READS = ()


def assistant_value(n):
    """Activation inside an assistant reply, `n` tokens after the role word."""
    if n == 0:
        return ROLE_WORD_VALUE
    for limit, value in ASSISTANT_TABLE:
        if n < limit:
            return value
    return ASSISTANT_DEEP


def token_offset(tok):
    if regex.search(r"\p{Han}", tok):
        return HAN_OFFSET
    if regex.fullmatch(r"[^\p{L}\p{N}]+", tok):
        return PUNCT_OFFSET
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, "none", 0, False)  # new document: no turn open
    _, role, n, opened = carry
    if tok == "<|im_start|>":
        role, n, opened = "none", 0, True
    elif opened and tok in ("user", "assistant"):
        role, n, opened = tok, 0, False
    elif tok == "<|im_end|>":
        role, n, opened = "none", 0, False
    else:
        opened = False
        n += 1
    carry = (doc, role, n, opened)
    if role == "assistant":
        value = assistant_value(n)
    elif role == "user":
        value = USER_VALUE
    else:
        value = NONE_VALUE
    return carry, value + token_offset(tok)

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 5177 (down_proj component 5177), as a line-break rule.

The component is essentially one MLP hidden unit of layer 15 (its input reads
hidden unit 5177 almost alone), so its activation is a signed, heavy-tailed
signal. Its largest positive values come at the line break that closes a
heading-like line: a short, Title-Case line ("Compliance and Regulatory
Requirements:" or "Different Models Have Different Purposes") with no closing
sentence punctuation. Most other tokens sit near the component's mean.

This program predicts that: at a newline that ends a heading-like line it
predicts a positive level, and everywhere else the mean level. It explains
only a sliver of the variance (about 0.1% on training text); the bulk of the
activation depends on context this simple rule cannot see.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

HEADING_LEVEL = 0.26  # mean activation at a line break after a heading-like line
OTHER_LEVEL = -0.05  # the component's typical value everywhere else


def is_heading(line: str) -> bool:
    """A short Title-Case line with no closing sentence punctuation, or a markdown heading."""
    words = line.split()
    if line.startswith("#"):
        return True
    if not 2 <= len(words) <= 12:
        return False
    if line.rstrip()[-1:] in ".?!,;":
        return False
    return all(w[:1].isupper() or w[:1].isdigit() for w in words)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # carry: the text of the current line so far, cleared at each newline and document start
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    line = "" if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if "\n" in token:
        value = HEADING_LEVEL if is_heading(line) else OTHER_LEVEL
        return "", value
    return (line + token)[-200:], OTHER_LEVEL

What it does: it goes negative on the head noun of an adjective-noun phrase, the noun
right after an adjective modifier, as in "the best [way]", "a good [price]", "a small
[amount]", "Required [parameter]". It is strongest after qualitative, evaluative or
size adjectives, and stronger again when a determiner or quantifier opens the phrase
("the best", "some other", "the most significant"). Generic category nouns ("thing",
"way", "part", "approach", "amount", "version") are negative after any word. Elsewhere
it stays near zero. Nouns after nouns (compounds) and nouns with a determiner directly
before them are about zero.

spread comes from contexts a word list cannot see, so the program is a readable summary of
the main trend, not a full account.
"""

from wordnet import parts_of_speech

READS = ()

# Qualitative, evaluative, size and quantity adjectives.
QUALITY_ADJECTIVES = frozenset(
    """best good bad worst better great important significant correct similar different
    required additional previous big small large little high highest low lower strong wide
    complete simple easy safe hard early late new main major key basic critical interesting
    reasonable preferred efficient latest healthy minimal serious usual alternative certain
    various desired existing related possible useful general specific common normal real
    original unique effective perfect fixed popular initial recent""".split()
)

# Words that open a noun phrase: "the", "a", "this", "some", "more", "most", ...
OPENERS = frozenset(
    """the a an this that these those some any more most other our my their your his its
    no every each all many several such""".split()
)

# Words that wordnet tags as adjectives but that act as function words here.
FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    """on all such each any some about after many only just both through under own up
    several into over from with between without within upon during across
    against among""".split()
)

# Generic category nouns that take a complement: "way to", "part of", "amount of".
GENERIC_NOUNS = frozenset(
    """thing things stuff ones way ways part parts aspect aspects approach approaches
    method methods technique techniques amount amounts level levels kind kinds type types
    version versions stage stages option options case cases choice choices issue issues
    factor factors point points area areas element elements feature features form forms
    source sources material materials topic topics concept concepts""".split()
)


def _word(token_string):
    return token_string.strip().lower()


def _has_pos(word, pos):
    return word.isalpha() and pos in (parts_of_speech(word) or set())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    word = _word(tokens[t])
    # The words before this one, if they are in the same document.
    prev = _word(tokens[t - 1]) if t >= 1 and docs[t - 1] == docs[t] else ""
    prev2 = _word(tokens[t - 2]) if t >= 2 and docs[t - 2] == docs[t] else ""

            value -= 1.3 if opened else 0.3

    return carry, value
